summary: Contract 5.3 and section 7 are implemented in full. OwnerGrid: Void cells come from the arena shape (cell center outside the rounded square), CountOf is O(1) and exact for every byte value, Version changes with the content, FillDisc and Neutralize are in. GridRaster: an allocation-free Amanatides-Woo walker (4-connected; a crossing parameter is computed straight from the crossed lattice line, never accumulated, so axis-aligned times are exact and a segment that ends on an edge gives u = 1 exactly; a cell entered at u = 1 is included; a corner tie visits the x-neighbour, then the diagonal). TraverseFrom covers the event engine: inclusive [0, uMax], a start on an edge enters at U = 0, negative and -0.0 tMax are clamped, one diagonal entry at a corner tie. FirstEntry, RasterPolyline, and RasterPolygon / CountInterior run a scanline over an active edge table (half-open y rule, non-zero winding, per-thread scratch). CaptureSolver.Compute is the one-large-flood implementation of section 7 on a pooled per-thread flag buffer keyed by grid size: ReachAfter by scanline span fill, then the step (iii) multi-source flood, then Rim, then a table-driven ascending collect into an exact-size result. Step (iii) runs as a span fill too; see contract_issues. GridQueries: NearestOwned is an exact Chebyshev ring search with the (r - 0.5) * CellSize bound; IsNeutralDisc. 63 A2 tests pass (dotnet), and the shared Core suite is 159/159. Every capture scenario (C1-C7, purity, pocket-only) and 325 random cases (full arena and a small arena where B is clamped to the grid) are checked against ReferenceCapture, a direct two-flood implementation of the section 7 definition written in the test file. Perf, worst case: a rim loop enclosing 88 % of the arena, box 506 x 506, 230,704 captured cells. .NET 9 Release: 1.33 ms average, 1.10 ms min. Opposite-corner box: 0.63 ms. Debug build (the dotnet test default): about 3.7 to 4.2 ms average.
api_additions: GridRaster.CornerTieEpsilon: public const double 1e-12, the corner tie tolerance |tMaxX - tMaxY| shared by TraverseSegment and TraverseFrom.

Internal only (not public API): struct SegmentWalker (the allocation-free TraverseSegment iterator used by FirstEntry, RasterPolyline, RasterPolygon and CaptureSolver), GridRaster.CrossingParam and CheckFinite, and OwnerGrid.GetDiscCellRange (shared by FillDisc and IsNeutralDisc).
contract_issues: 10.1 RasterPolygon 'full raster vs area + perimeter * CellSize within 5 %' cannot hold for an axis-aligned square of side 4. The supercover band straddles the edge, so the full raster is (side + CellSize)^2 = area + perimeter * CellSize / 2 + CellSize^2: 17.02 u^2 against 18, which is -5.5 %. The tolerance holds from a side of about 5.3 u. The test asserts the exact column x row count for axis-aligned squares (sides 4, 7.25, 16), the contract tolerance for sides 7.25 and 16, and the contract tolerance for a side-4 square rotated by 30 degrees (passes). Suggested wording: 'area + perimeter * CellSize / 2 within 5 %', or 'side >= 6 u'.

Section 7 step (iii) says 'a multi-source BFS'. It is implemented as a multi-source scanline span fill over the same cells (non-own trail cells and U cells) from the same seeds, so the reachable set is identical and the code runs several times faster on large boxes. Equality with the definition is checked against an independent two-flood reference on every C test and on 325 random cases. The seeds also include non-own trail cells on the border of B, because those cells are ReachBefore seeds by definition. This can only happen when B is clamped to the grid border, which never happens in a round (R1).

Section 7 step 5 (Rim by 4-adjacency, normative, unchanged) leaves two kinds of trail cells neutral: the outer cell at a convex corner of the trail, and the outer stair cells of a diagonal trail segment. The result is a one-cell notch or sawtooth along the captured edge. It is cosmetic (the territory blur hides it; C1 area stays within 3 %). Rim by 8-adjacency would fill them, if the user wants that.

5.3 OwnerGrid.Version 'increments on every mutation' is implemented as 'on every content change', like A1's CellMask. Version stays the same for a Set to the current owner, a Set on a Void cell, and a Neutralize of an owner with no cells. FillDisc goes through Set (one increment per changed cell); Neutralize increments once per call that changes something.

5.3 does not say whether RasterPolyline and RasterPolygon clear their output. Both ADD to the mask and never clear it, which lets a caller rasterize straight into an existing mask; a caller that reuses a scratch mask must Clear it first (A4's EventResolver already does). RasterPolyline skips Void cells, because R1 says Void cells are never walls.

5.3 OwnerGrid.Neutralize: 'changed' may be null. It is cleared first, then receives the freed indices in ascending order (A4 already clears it and sorts it, which is harmless). OwnerGrid.Set(index, Void) throws ArgumentException, because Void is fixed by the arena shape and assigning it would corrupt ArenaCellCount. Set on a Void cell is ignored, as specified.

5.3 TraverseSegment's 'first cell containing a + Tiny*(b-a)' is implemented as floor, except that a coordinate lying exactly on a lattice line with negative motion on that axis starts in the lower cell. This gives the same cell as the formula up to rounding, and it stays correct when Tiny*(b-a) is below the ulp of a (short segments far from the origin). Cells outside the grid are skipped (never passed to the visitor). A segment that starts far outside the grid is clipped to the grid box grown by one cell, so the walk length stays bounded. Non-finite points throw ArgumentException, which turns a NaN bug elsewhere into an exception instead of a hang.

Results when a query finds nothing (contract silent): FirstEntry gives u = 0. NearestOwned gives target = p and distance = +inf, and returns false at once when the owner has no cell. IsNeutralDisc ignores Void cells and the parts of the disc outside the grid.
open_issues: Unity EditMode was not run by A2 (this task did not require Unity). The tests use only NUnit 3.5 features (Test, TestCase, SetUp, Category, Assert.That / AreEqual / IsTrue / IsFalse / Throws / Fail, CollectionAssert.AreEqual) plus value tuples and a local function in the test code. The allocation test uses GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread and is compiled only outside Unity (#if !UNITY_5_3_OR_NEWER). Gate A should confirm the counts in Unity.

Perf test Capture_Perf_FullSizeBox ([Category("Perf")]) logs average and min times and asserts under 10 ms in the dotnet loop. Under UNITY_5_3_OR_NEWER the bound is 30 ms, because the Editor runs Mono with Debug code optimization and the 3 ms budget applies to players. In dotnet Debug the worst case measures about 3.7 to 4.2 ms on average, in Release 1.33 ms. Android Medium (IL2CPP ARM64, 8 ms budget) is not measured here (B6 probe).

GR-Edge emulates the section 6 head traversal directly (Arena.Step per tick, TraverseFrom from the current cell, a state check on every visited entry including the one at U = 0, Cell = last entry) instead of running the Simulation, as the task allowed. It covers +x, -x, +y and -y at 30, 60 and 144 Hz for exits and returns: exactly one transition, at 1/12 s within 1e-9 s. The Simulation-level R5 and GR-Edge equivalents belong to A4.

CaptureSolver scans all 512 x 512 owner bytes once per call to find the bounding box of the player's cells (about 0.1 ms). A per-owner bounding box kept incrementally by OwnerGrid could remove that scan. A stale, larger box would still give the same result, because any box that contains the bbox + 1 does. Not needed for the budget.

The CaptureSolver and scanline buffers are [ThreadStatic] (CaptureSolver: one dictionary per thread keyed by grid size; for 512 x 512 that is a 256 KB flag buffer plus a 128 KB span stack that grows on demand), so parallel test runners stay safe and a round allocates nothing after the first capture apart from the returned array.
